subject: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@vectorscale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Samira —

We need to escalate a recurring production issue with the VectorScale -> Redwood EventBridge connector. Over the last 48 hours we've seen a spike in duplicate event deliveries and increased end-to-end latency impacting a handful of your customers on the VectorScale managed pipeline. The duplicates are causing downstream dedupe backpressure and queueing on our Dedicated pools.

What we need from you urgently:
- Confirm a point-of-contact from VectorScale who can be on a short bridge (phone + slack) today.
- Review the attached error dump (vectorscale-eventbridge-errors-0401.txt) and the diagnostic bundle (vectorscale-diagnostics-0401.zip).
- Agree a temporary mitigation (rate-limit or signature validation) and a plan for a canary patch.

Internal folks: Ben and Jordan are looped — Ben can lead the bridge ops, Jordan can review connector config changes.

I recommend we define acceptance criteria for the SLA handoff (target dedupe rate < 0.5%, p95 latency < 200ms for event ACK) and schedule a 60-min alignment call to sign the partner oncall handshake.

Attachments: vectorscale-eventbridge-errors-0401.txt (excerpt), vectorscale-diagnostics-0401.zip (traces)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Samira Khan <samira@vectorscale.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: VectorScale Support <support@vectorscale.io>, Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 09:40 AM -0700
Subject: Re: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We opened ticket #48912 in our support system and assigned Abe as the lead engineer on this. He'll start by validating the signature verification and retry semantics on our side.

Short answers:
- POC for the bridge today: Abe Sullivan (abe@vectorscale.io), available after 10:30 PT.
- We'll review the attachments now — can you confirm whether the duplicates correlate with a specific model or route on your side?
- We'll propose a temporary rate-limit config and a permanent fix plan within 4 business hours.

Ticket: https://support.vectorscale.io/tickets/48912

Samira Khan
Director, Partner Integrations
VectorScale
samira@vectorscale.io
From: Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@vectorscale.io>
Cc: VectorScale Support <support@vectorscale.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:18 AM -0700
Subject: Re: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Marissa, Samira —

I've pulled the diagnostics and reproduced duplicate webhook deliveries when our retry window overlaps with delayed ACKs from Redwood's connector (we see 2-3 retries within a 30s window). Two immediate mitigations we can propose:

1) Apply a conservative jittered exponential backoff on our retry policy for your EventBridge route (temporary, can be deployed in <30m).
2) Enable signature verification on inbound events to allow Redwood to detect and drop duplicates earlier (requires a small config change and TLS key sync).

I attached a short diagnostic (vectorscale-diagnostics-0401.zip) and a proposed rate-limit patch. I'm happy to join a bridge at 11:00 PT to push the temporary change — please confirm.

Attachments: vectorscale-diagnostics-0401.zip

—Abe
Abe Sullivan
Senior Engineer, Integrations
VectorScale
abe@vectorscale.io
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:35 AM -0700
Subject: Re: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Marissa / Ben —

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:18 AM Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io> wrote:
> Marissa, Samira —
> 
> I've pulled the diagnostics and reproduced duplicate webhook deliveries when our retry window overlaps with delayed ACKs from Redwood's connector (we see 2-3 retries within a 30s window).

Quick internal notes / plan:
- We can enable a dedupe TTL on the connector side (version 2.3.1) that will drop repeated event IDs within a 60s window. That is low-risk and reversible.
- I'll put Jonas on a canary deployment to a single Dedicated pool (pool-3) and monitor p95 lat / duplicate rate for 6 hours.
- If VectorScale applies the temporary backoff, we expect duplicates to fall immediately; if not, our dedupe TTL will limit customer impact while we patch root cause.

Ben: please coordinate the bridge and include CS for any customer-facing comms. Abe: if you can push the small rate-limit config we can flip the TTL on in parallel.

Jordan
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io>
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 09:14 AM -0700
Subject: Re: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Marissa / team —

I've deployed the dedupe-ttl (60s) to a canary on pool-3 at 08:45 PT. Early telemetry shows a 31% reduction in visible duplicate deliveries and p95 ACK latency down from 360ms to 185ms for the canary traffic slice. Screenshot attached: redwood-canary-perf-0402.png

Next asks:
- VectorScale to confirm they pushed the jittered exponential backoff (Abe noted he can at 11:00 PT yesterday; please confirm applied window).
- We need acceptance criteria from Product/PS: I'll consider the canary successful if duplicate rate < 0.5% and p95 latency < 200ms over a 6-hour window.

I've also prepared a minimal patch for the connector to improve ACK processing; that can ship as a 1.2.1 hotfix after we validate canary.

Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@vectorscale.io>, Abe Sullivan <abe@vectorscale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 03:40 PM -0700
Subject: Re: VectorScale EventBridge connector: support escalation and SLA handoff

Thanks everyone —

Summary / next steps (agreed):
1) VectorScale confirms they applied the jittered exponential backoff on 4/1 at ~11:05 PT (Samira/Abe please confirm in reply).
2) Redwood keeps the dedupe-ttl canary active on pool-3 for 6 more hours; Jonas will surface a pass/fail by end of day.
3) If canary meets acceptance (duplicates < 0.5%, p95 < 200ms) we schedule the connector 1.2.1 hotfix rollout and update the partner SLA doc.
4) Joint 60-minute alignment call to finalize the partner oncall handshake, escalation matrix, and 24/7 rostering. Proposed slot: Mon Apr 5, 10:00 PT — accept?

Attachments: vectorscale-sla-proposal-draft.pdf (draft partner SLA clauses)

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-vectorscale-handshake (working doc), HUBSPOT-63452

Samira / Abe — please confirm item #1 and whether VectorScale can commit to a 4-hour SLA for initial mitigation in the future.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
